summary.headline: PSP Projects Q4FY26 revenue rose 66% YoY to INR1,115 crores, but a INR29 crore Kashi ECL provision kept FY26 PAT flat at INR55 crores.
summary.overview: Q4FY26 was the company's highest-ever quarterly revenue at INR1,115 crores (up 66% YoY), with EBITDA up 85% to INR60 crores and PAT up to INR21 crores. Reported margins were depressed by a INR29 crore expected credit loss provision on unbilled revenue from the Kashi project, which took other expenses from INR17 crores to INR46 crores. For FY26, revenue grew 25% to INR3,149 crores, EBITDA rose 5% to INR189 crores with margin down to 6% from 7.14%, and PAT was flat-to-down at INR55 crores. Order book reached INR13,447 crores (up 85%) after record order inflow of INR10,925 crores, 85% of it from the Adani group.

segments.name: Adani group (in-house) orders
segments.commentary: Adani group accounted for 85% of FY26 order inflow and about INR9,000 crores (67%) of the current INR13,400 crore order book. Management says materials are pass-through on Adani contracts.

segments.name: External / non-group orders
segments.commentary: External projects are about 33-43% of the order book (about INR4,300 crores per the Q&A). Government projects fell to about 25% of the order book from 43% a year earlier.

segments.name: Precast manufacturing
segments.commentary: Current precast capacity is 3 million sq ft per year. Management says expansion to 1.5x would need only INR15-20 crores of equipment since sheds are already built. Project 90 was pre-executed in 148 days.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance is about INR4,500 crores, reiterated by management.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 7-8%, with management saying it can move 1% plus or minus; the Q&A confirmed 7-8% as the band for the next two years.
Management expects to be debt-free within about two to three quarters, with interest cost of about INR11-12 crores per quarter falling toward nil.
Working capital: trade receivable days are expected to fall to about 60 days (60-70 days per the Q&A) from about 94 days.

Order inflow is expected at INR5,000-6,000 crores from the group plus INR1,000-2,000 crores from outside in FY27. The bid pipeline is about INR6,500 crores, of which about INR5,000 crores is group and INR1,500 crores external.
Capex for FY27 is expected at about INR120-150 crores (roughly 2-4% of revenue), with quarterly lumpiness possible.
Employee cost is expected to grow about 2-4% (per the Q&A), with operating leverage as revenue rises.
Medium-term goal is 20-25% growth per year, with a target of about INR9,000-10,000 crores revenue by FY30 (per the analyst's recap, not restated by management).
capex_capacity: FY26 capex was INR192 crores; Q4FY26 capex was INR40 crores. Gross block is INR764 crores and net block INR412 crores.
Precast plant capacity is 3 million sq ft per year; management sees no major expansion needed at the current pace.
Projects under execution: 94 ongoing across Gujarat, UP, Rajasthan, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Delhi NCR; over 256 completed to date.

Mumbai projects (Mahim, Matunga) are at early foundation stage; Matunga is at sheet piling. Tree-cutting approvals are a delay risk. Management says about INR10,000 crores of the order book is at peak execution pace.
Dharoi Dam Phase 1 was handed over and Phase 2 is in finishing. SMC RCC is complete and RVNL core and shell is complete.
demand_pricing: Order book INR13,447 crores (+85% YoY), with group projects at 67% and external at 43% per the CEO's figures (these overlap; the Q&A split is 67% Adani and 33% non-Adani).
Record FY26 order inflow of INR10,925 crores, 85% from Adani group. Major wins include SVPI Airport Ahmedabad development, Matunga Rehab Building Mumbai, and Shri Ambaji Mata Temple extension.

Key outstanding orders: Shree Ambaji Mata Temple INR966 crores, SMC Highrise INR731 crores, Human & Biological Science Gallery INR254 crores, GIFT City Fintech Building INR261 crores, Dharoi Dam INR223 crores, Gati Shakti Vishwavidyalaya INR216 crores, Sabarmati Riverfront Phase II INR218 crores, GIFT City residential INR210 crores.

Commonwealth Games-linked tenders (about INR7,000-8,000 crores potential, per analyst) are expected to be announced but had not been formally released; management expects them 'anytime in this quarter'.
Mobilisation advances of INR814 crores from the group are interest-free. Management says the group advance will fund most working capital.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY27 revenue guidance of INR4,500 crores and FY30 target of INR9,000-10,000 crores changed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management stuck to INR4,500 crores for FY27 and said margins are improving; Q4 EBITDA margin excluding the INR30 crore provision would be about 8%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Kashi ECL provision and will more come?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR29 crore provision was made because receivables beyond one year must be provided for. Management is still chasing the UP Medical College accounts through government channels and does not expect major further ECL provisions.

qa_highlights.question: How much UP Medical College money is outstanding?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR60 crores unbilled and INR40 crores trade receivable across seven projects. INR40 crores of GST invoices are pending, and final certification is awaited.

qa_highlights.question: Will PAT margin reach 4-5%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects to be debt-free within about two to three quarters, which would remove about INR41-45 crores of annual interest. It said PAT margin could reach 3-4% and that 4.5-5% is the target for next year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook and receivable days?
qa_highlights.answer: Receivable days were about 90-100 at March 2026 because most revenue was booked in February and March. Management expects them to fall to around 60-70 days, with collection in April.

qa_highlights.question: Is capex/depreciation going to stay at 3% of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 capex is about INR120-150 crores, with possible flexibility to about 2% of revenue. Depreciation is expected to keep rising from new assets, so it cannot be cut.

qa_highlights.question: What is the SDB receivable status?
qa_highlights.answer: The client has just started operations. About INR90 crores of principal is in receivables, with interest billed separately. Management expects resolution during FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Adani mix or the ongoing war pressure margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said most orders are Adani with pass-through materials, so it sees no major war-related margin risk. Only SMC and RVNL may see small impact.

risks_watch: Receivables jumped to INR928 crores (about 90-100 days) at March 2026; watch April-June collections against management's 60-70 day target.
Collection risk on UP Medical College (about INR60 crores unbilled and INR40 crores receivable) and the remaining Kashi and SDB balances. Further ECL provisions are possible.
Margin guidance (7-8%) depends on no further provisions. Q4 margin was depressed by the INR29 crore provision, and FY26 EBITDA margin fell to 6%.
Concentration risk: about 67% of the order book is Adani group. Mobilisation advances of INR814 crores are a funding source; a slowdown in group inflows would matter.
Execution risk in Mumbai (tree-cutting approvals, monsoon, labour availability in Q1-Q2 FY27), and the timing of Commonwealth-linked tenders.
Debt-free target and interest saving depend on collections; gross debt of about INR317 crores (INR43 crores long-term plus INR274 crores short-term) remains.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, visibility and the FY27 revenue target, but cautious and somewhat defensive on margins, the Kashi/UP receivables and the timing of collections. Management repeatedly framed the 7-8% margin band as conservative and pointed to group advances and pass-through terms as mitigants.
